query: Who was Nephi?

documents.text: And Nephi, who was the father of Nephi, who had the charge of the records, did not return to the land of Zarahemla, and could nowhere be found in all the land.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 2:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records the people forgetting earlier signs, hardening their hearts, and growing in wickedness as years 95–100 pass, with time reckoned from the sign of Christ’s coming. Nephi, keeper of the records, does not return to Zarahemla and cannot be found. In the thirteenth year wars intensify with numerous Gadianton robbers; converted Lamanites unite with Nephites, are numbered as Nephites, and fight for safety and worship. Fighting continues through years 14–15 with shifting advantages and increasing afflictions.

documents.text: I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents, therefore I was taught somewhat in all the learning of my father; and having seen many afflictions in the course of my days, nevertheless, having been highly favored of the Lord in all my days; yea, having had a great knowledge of the goodness and the mysteries of God, therefore I make a record of my proceedings in my days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 1:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Nephi’s introduction to his record and language, and sets the scene in the first year of Zedekiah at Jerusalem. Lehi prays, sees a pillar of fire, and receives a vision of heaven, a descending figure with twelve others, and a book. Reading it, he prophesies Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, and testifies of a coming Messiah. The people mock and seek Lehi’s life.

documents.text: And now I, Nephi, proceed to give an account upon these plates of my proceedings, and my reign and ministry; wherefore, to proceed with mine account, I must speak somewhat of the things of my father, and also of my brethren.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 10:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Lehi prophesying of Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, the Jews’ return, and the coming Messiah about six hundred years after leaving Jerusalem. He mentions prophets testifying, a forerunner who baptizes in Bethabara beyond Jordan, and the Messiah’s death and resurrection with manifestation to Gentiles by the Holy Ghost. It covers Israel scattered and gathered like an olive tree. Nephi desires revelation and warns of judgment and uncleanness.

documents.text: Wherefore, it came to pass that I, Nephi, did take my family, and also Zoram and his family, and Sam, mine elder brother and his family, and Jacob and Joseph, my younger brethren, and also my sisters, and all those who would go with me. documents.text: And it came to pass that I, Nephi, being exceedingly young, nevertheless being large in stature, and also having great desires to know of the mysteries of God, wherefore, I did cry unto the Lord; and behold he did visit me, and did soften my heart that I did believe all the words which had been spoken by my father; wherefore, I did not rebel against him like unto my brothers.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 2:16** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 24 verses and records the Lord warning Lehi in a dream to flee Jerusalem; Lehi departs with Sariah and sons, leaving property, and travels near the Red Sea to a valley where he builds an altar and names the river Laman. Laman and Lemuel murmur; Lehi rebukes them. Nephi prays, believes, and teaches Sam. The Lord promises prosperity and a land of promise for obedience, and foretells consequences and roles for rebellion.

documents.text: And it came to pass in the fifty and third year of the reign of the judges, Helaman died, and his eldest son Nephi began to reign in his stead. documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 3:37** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records contention and dissensions in years 43–48, including migrations from Zarahemla to the land northward, settlement near large waters, cement building, shipping timber, and growth of cities and temples. It notes extensive Nephite recordkeeping and later Nephite decline. Helaman judges with justice, names sons Nephi and Lehi, and peace returns while Gadianton’s secret combinations persist. Many join the church by baptism; later pride brings persecution. Helaman dies; Nephi succeeds.

documents.text: And now there were some among the people, who said that Nephi was a prophet.

documents.text: And it came to pass that after my father had made an end of speaking to the sons and daughters of Laman, he caused the sons and daughters of Lemuel to be brought before him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 4:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Lehi blessing the children of Laman and Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Sam, giving commandments about prosperity and being cut off. Lehi dies and is buried. Laman, Lemuel, and Ishmael’s sons become angry with Nephi. Nephi explains his writing purpose, recounts divine help, angels and visions, and offers prayers for deliverance, strength, and trust in God rather than man.

documents.text: I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents, therefore I was taught somewhat in all the learning of my father; and having seen many afflictions in the course of my days, nevertheless, having been highly favored of the Lord in all my days; yea, having had a great knowledge of the goodness and the mysteries of God, therefore I make a record of my proceedings in my days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 1:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Nephi’s introduction to his record and language, and sets the scene in the first year of Zedekiah at Jerusalem. Lehi prays, sees a pillar of fire, and receives a vision of heaven, a descending figure with twelve others, and a book. Reading it, he prophesies Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, and testifies of a coming Messiah. The people mock and seek Lehi’s life.

documents.text: And it came to pass that my father did speak unto them in the valley of Lemuel, with power, being filled with the Spirit, until their frames did shake before him. And he did confound them, that they durst not utter against him; wherefore, they did as he commanded them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 2:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 24 verses and records the Lord warning Lehi in a dream to flee Jerusalem; Lehi departs with Sariah and sons, leaving property, and travels near the Red Sea to a valley where he builds an altar and names the river Laman. Laman and Lemuel murmur; Lehi rebukes them. Nephi prays, believes, and teaches Sam. The Lord promises prosperity and a land of promise for obedience, and foretells consequences and roles for rebellion.

documents.text: And it had come to pass that my father spake unto her, saying: I know that I am a visionary man; for if I had not seen the things of God in a vision I should not have known the goodness of God, but had tarried at Jerusalem, and had perished with my brethren.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 5:4** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Lehi’s family rejoicing when Nephi and his brothers return from Jerusalem with the brass plates. Sariah fears her sons have died, complains against Lehi, then is comforted and testifies the Lord protected them. The family offers sacrifices and thanks. Lehi searches the plates, finding the books of Moses, Jewish history to Zedekiah, prophecies including Jeremiah, and his genealogy from Joseph. Lehi prophesies the plates will endure and bless his seed.

query: What happened to the people of Ammonihah?

documents.text: And thus ended the eleventh year of the judges, the Lamanites having been driven out of the land, and the people of Ammonihah were destroyed; yea, every living soul of the Ammonihahites was destroyed, and also their great city, which they said God could not destroy, because of its greatness.

documents.context:

This chapter contains 30 verses and records Lamanite armies approaching rebuilt Ammonihah and being thwarted by Moroni’s fortifications. Lamanite assaults fail; chief captains are slain and over a thousand die, while no Nephites are killed and about fifty are wounded. Amalickiah reacts with anger and oaths, while Nephites give thanks; the year ends with peace and church prosperity under Helaman, Shiblon, Corianton, and Ammon."

documents.text: And again, I, Alma, having been commanded of God that I should take Amulek and go forth and preach again unto this people, or the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, it came to pass as I began to preach unto them, they began to contend with me, saying:
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Alma 9:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Alma, commanded by God, preaching again in Ammonihah with Amulek. The people contend, question his authority, and attempt to seize him. Alma recounts Lehi’s deliverance, warns that prosperity depends on keeping commandments, and calls them to repent or face destruction, including invasion by Lamanites. He cites angelic warnings and prophesies the Son of God’s coming to redeem the repentant. The Lord prevents Alma’s imprisonment; Amulek begins preaching."

documents.text: And it came to pass after they had thus suffered for many days, (and it was on the twelfth day, in the tenth month, in the tenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi) that the chief judge over the land of Ammonihah and many of their teachers and their lawyers went in unto the prison where Alma and Amulek were bound with cords.

documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 12:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Abinadi returning in disguise to prophesy against King Noah’s people, warning of bondage, afflictions, and Noah’s death unless they repent. The people seize Abinadi and bring him to Noah, who imprisons him and consults the priests. The priests question Abinadi, quoting Isaiah, and he condemns them for perverting the Lord’s ways, neglecting the law of Moses, and seeking riches and immorality. Abinadi cites commandments from Sinai and accuses them of not teaching or keeping them.

query: How many days was Jesus in the tomb?

documents.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 11:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture."
**Verse**: "Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already."

documents.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.

documents.text: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.

It argues that denying resurrection makes faith and preaching vain, then outlines resurrection order and Christ’s reign until death is destroyed. It mentions baptism for the dead, warns against corrupting associations, explains resurrection bodies, and commands steadfast labor.

Jesus heals many and commands silence, with an Isaiah citation. He casts out a demon from a blind, mute man, answers Beelzebub accusations, warns about blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, teaches about words and fruit, refuses a sign except Jonah, describes returning unclean spirits, and identifies doers of God’s will as family."
**Verse**: "For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth."

documents.context: The following passage is from **John 2:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Jesus turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana, leading his disciples to believe. It notes his brief stay in Capernaum with his mother, brethren, and disciples. At Passover in Jerusalem, he drives merchants and money changers from the temple and is questioned for a sign. query: Who translated the Book of Mormon?

It recounts calling Joseph Smith and others to establish the church, translate the Book of Mormon, and proclaim the gospel, with promises of forgiveness for repentance and fulfillment of the Lord’s word.

documents.text: Two days after the arrival of Mr. Cowdery (being the 7th of April) I commenced to translate the Book of Mormon, and he began to write for me.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joseph Smith—History 1:67** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 75 verses and records Joseph Smith’s purpose for writing (1838), his birth and family moves to Palmyra and Manchester, and local religious revivals. It recounts his 1820 prayer and vision of two Personages, instruction to join no sect, and ensuing persecution. It covers Moroni’s 1823 visits about gold plates, Urim and Thummim, annual meetings, and warnings. It records obtaining and safeguarding the plates (1827), moving to Pennsylvania, early translation, Martin Harris’s Anthon visit, Oliver Cowdery as scribe, and John the Baptist conferring Aaronic Priesthood and commanding baptism (May 1829).

documents.text: "I went to the city of New York, and presented the characters which had been translated, with the translation thereof, to Professor Charles Anthon, a gentleman celebrated for his literary attainments. Professor Anthon stated that the translation was correct, more so than any he had before seen translated from the Egyptian. I then showed him those which were not yet translated, and he said that they were Egyptian, Chaldaic, Assyriac, and Arabic; and he said they were true characters. He gave me a certificate, certifying to the people of Palmyra that they were true characters, and that the translation of such of them as had been translated was also correct. I took the certificate and put it into my pocket, and was just leaving the house, when Mr. Anthon called me back, and asked me how the young man found out that there were gold plates in the place where he found them. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions.

documents.text: Therefore ye must always pray unto the Father in my name;
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 18:19** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Jesus instituting the sacrament with bread and wine among the disciples and multitude, commanding it be done in remembrance of his body and blood, and promising his Spirit to those who always remember him. He commands watchfulness and continual prayer, family prayer, meeting often, and welcoming seekers. He instructs disciples to forbid unworthy partaking without casting people out, to minister and pray for them, warns against disputations, gives disciples power to give the Holy Ghost, and ascends into heaven.

documents.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 6:13** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus teaching to give alms, pray, and fast in secret rather than for public display, including the Lord’s Prayer and commands to forgive others. It contrasts earthly and heavenly treasures, discusses the single eye and serving God rather than mammon, and instructs not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: Pray without ceasing.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Thessalonians 5:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 28 verses and covers the day of the Lord coming unexpectedly, urging believers to watch and be sober, equipped with faith, love, and hope. It calls them to comfort and edify one another, respect leaders, maintain peace, and practice patience and good toward all. It commands rejoicing, continual prayer, thanksgiving, not quenching the Spirit, valuing prophecy, testing all things, and avoiding evil, and closes with a sanctification prayer, greetings, and a charge to read the letter.

documents.text: And now Father, I pray unto thee for them, and also for all those who shall believe on their words, that they may believe in me, that I may be in them as thou, Father, art in me, that we may be one.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 19:23** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 36 verses and records the people gathering again after Jesus ascends, as the twelve chosen disciples teach, organize the multitude, and lead prayer in Jesus’s name. Nephi is baptized and then baptizes the other disciples; the Holy Ghost falls on them with fire, and angels minister. Jesus appears, commands kneeling and prayer, and prays to the Father for the disciples and future believers, noting their great faith."
**Verse**: "And now Father, I pray unto thee for them, and also for all those who shall believe on their words, that they may believe in me, that I may be in them as thou, Father, art in me, that we may be one."

documents.text: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Luke 18:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Jesus’ parables of the persistent widow and the unjust judge, and the Pharisee and the publican praying in the temple. It describes Jesus blessing infants and teaching about receiving God’s kingdom like a child. A ruler asks about eternal life; Jesus cites commandments and tells him to sell possessions and follow him, teaching on riches and salvation. Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection, then heals a blind beggar near Jericho."
**Verse**: "And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;"

documents.text: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 17:9** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Jesus praying to the Father to glorify him, affirming authority to give eternal life and defining it as knowing the true God and Jesus Christ. He prays for the disciples, not the world, asking their protection, joy, sanctification by truth, and unity. He notes one lost “son of perdition,” sends them into the world, and prays also for future believers to be one and share his glory and love."
**Verse**: "I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine."

documents.text: And they did kneel down with the church, and pray to the Father in the name of Christ, saying:
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Moroni 4:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 3 verses and records the manner elders and priests administer the sacrament bread to the church according to Christ’s commandments, kneeling with the congregation and praying to the Father in Christ’s name to bless and sanctify the bread, for participants to remember Christ’s body, take upon them his name, always remember him, keep his commandments, and have his Spirit with them."
**Verse**: "And they did kneel down with the church, and pray to the Father in the name of Christ, saying:"

query: What does scripture say about repentance?

documents.text: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 3:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Peter and John healing a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful, causing public amazement in Solomon’s porch. Peter attributes the miracle to faith in Jesus Christ, recounts Israel’s rejection of Jesus before Pilate, and testifies of Jesus’ resurrection. He calls for repentance, cites Moses and the prophets, references the Abrahamic covenant, and states that Jesus is sent first to bless Israel by turning people from iniquities.

documents.text: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 8:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records persecution after Stephen’s death, with believers scattered from Jerusalem while Saul imprisons many. Philip preaches in Samaria, performs healings and exorcisms, and many are baptized, including Simon the sorcerer. Peter and John confer the Holy Ghost by laying on hands; Simon is rebuked for offering money. Philip later baptizes an Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road and then preaches from Azotus to Caesarea.

documents.text: And the first fruits of repentance is baptism; and baptism cometh by faith unto the fulfilling the commandments; and the fulfilling the commandments bringeth remission of sins;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 8:25** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records an epistle from Mormon to Moroni addressing disputes about baptizing little children. Mormon reports seeking the Lord and teaches that little children are alive in Christ, not accountable for sin, and need no repentance or baptism. He defines baptism as for accountable sinners unto remission of sins and warns against perverting this doctrine. He also mentions conflict with the Lamanites and Nephite pride, spiritual decline, and impending destruction.

documents.text: And him that repenteth not of his sins, and confesseth them not, ye shall bring before the church, and do with him as the scripture saith unto you, either by commandment or by revelation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 64:12** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to church elders to overcome the world, repent, and forgive all men, with directions for church discipline of the unrepentant. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

documents.text: But if ye will repent and return unto the Lord your God I will turn away mine anger, saith the Lord; yea, thus saith the Lord, blessed are they who will repent and turn unto me, but wo unto him that repenteth not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 2:38** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 47 verses and records Pentecost in Jerusalem, when the apostles receive the Holy Ghost with wind and tongues like fire and speak in other languages heard by Jews from many regions. Peter addresses the crowd, cites Joel and David, proclaims Jesus’ crucifixion, resurrection, and exaltation, and calls for repentance and baptism. About three thousand are baptized; believers continue in teaching, fellowship, prayers, signs, shared goods, temple worship, and house-to-house breaking of bread.

documents.text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joel 2:13** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records an alarm in Zion about the day of the LORD and a great invading army bringing darkness and devastation. It commands repentance with fasting, assembly, and priestly intercession. The LORD promises pity, removal of the northern army, restoration of crops and rains, and renewal after locust loss. It foretells the Spirit poured on all flesh, cosmic signs, and deliverance for those calling on the LORD in Zion and Jerusalem.

documents.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Corinthians 7:10** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 16 verses and records Paul urging believers to cleanse themselves and pursue holiness, defending his conduct toward the Corinthians. He describes troubles in Macedonia and comfort received through Titus’s arrival and report of their desire, mourning, and zeal. Paul explains his earlier letter caused temporary sorrow leading to repentance, contrasts godly and worldly sorrow, notes their renewed obedience, and expresses joy, comfort, and confidence in them.

documents.text: Therefore, whoso repenteth and cometh unto me as a little child, him will I receive, for of such is the kingdom of God. Behold, for such I have laid down my life, and have taken it up again; therefore repent, and come unto me ye ends of the earth, and be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 9:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records a voice speaking to all the land, pronouncing woe and urging repentance after widespread destructions. It names cities destroyed by fire, sinking, burial, or flooding, including Zarahemla, Moroni, Moronihah, Gilgal, Onihah, Mocum, Jerusalem, Gadiandi, Gadiomnah, Jacob, Gimgimno, Jacobugath, Laman, Josh, Gad, and Kishkumen. Jesus Christ identifies himself, offers mercy and eternal life, fulfills the law of Moses, ends blood sacrifices, and commands offering a broken heart and contrite spirit.

documents.text: But I say unto you, O man, whosoever doeth this the same hath great cause to repent; and except he repenteth of that which he hath done he perisheth forever, and hath no interest in the kingdom of God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 4:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records King Benjamin’s people falling down, pleading for mercy through Christ’s atoning blood, and receiving joy and remission of sins. Benjamin commands belief in God, repentance, humility, prayer, and steadfast faith. He instructs them to live peaceably, teach children, and succor the poor by sharing substance, feeding, clothing, and visiting the sick, in wisdom and order, returning borrowed goods, watching thoughts, words, and deeds, and keeping commandments to avoid perishing.

documents.text: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 24:47** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 53 verses and records women finding Jesus’ empty tomb, two angels announcing his resurrection, and the report to the apostles; Peter visits the sepulchre. Jesus appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explains scriptures, is recognized in breaking bread, and vanishes. He appears to the gathered disciples, shows his hands and feet, eats food, commissions preaching repentance and remission of sins, promises power from on high, and ascends near Bethany.

documents.text: And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Helaman 12:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Mormon’s reflections on human unsteadiness: people prosper, forget God, and require chastening by afflictions, death, famine, and pestilence. It states God’s power to command earth, mountains, waters, and the length of day, and to curse hidden treasures and individuals for iniquity. It declares repentance as the means of salvation and contrasts final outcomes of everlasting life versus damnation."
**Verse**: "And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared."

documents.text: Know ye that ye must come unto repentance, or ye cannot be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 7:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records Mormon addressing the spared remnant of the house of Israel. He states they are Israel and must repent to be saved, lay down weapons, and stop shedding blood unless God commands. He urges belief in Jesus Christ’s death and resurrection, teaching resurrection and judgment. He commands repentance and baptism, referencing additional records, and identifies them as Jacob’s remnant of the first covenant.

documents.text: And also the Spirit saith unto me, yea, crieth unto me with a mighty voice, saying: Go forth and say unto this people—Repent, for except ye repent ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of heaven.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Alma 5:51** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 62 verses and records Alma preaching in Zarahemla, recounting his father’s church in Mormon and deliverance from Noah’s people and the Lamanites. He questions the church about remembering captivity, experiencing a change of heart, and being judged by works. He commands repentance, humility, avoiding pride and persecution, caring for the poor, and producing good fruit. Alma testifies by the Spirit of Jesus Christ’s coming and invites all to be baptized."
**Verse**: "And also the Spirit saith unto me, yea, crieth unto me with a mighty voice, saying: Go forth and say unto this people—Repent, for except ye repent ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of heaven."

documents.text: But God hath made known unto our fathers that all men must repent.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:50** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: And now, my brethren, I would that, after ye have received so many witnesses, seeing that the holy scriptures testify of these things, ye come forth and bring fruit unto repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:30** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 3:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing in the Jordan as people confess sins, and warning Pharisees and Sadducees to produce worthy fruit. John describes one coming after him who baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire and brings judgment. Jesus comes from Galilee, is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a heavenly voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son.

documents.text: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jonah 3:10** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records the LORD commanding Jonah a second time to preach in Nineveh. Jonah goes to the great city and proclaims that in forty days Nineveh will be overthrown. The people believe God, fast, and wear sackcloth. The king decrees fasting for people and animals and calls for turning from evil and violence. God sees their repentance and does not bring the announced destruction.

documents.text: And he hath power given unto him from the Father to redeem them from their sins because of repentance; therefore he hath sent his angels to declare the tidings of the conditions of repentance, which bringeth unto the power of the Redeemer, unto the salvation of their souls.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 5:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 52 verses and records Nephi giving the judgment-seat to Cezoram and choosing to preach with Lehi amid corrupt government. Helaman’s counsel to his sons is quoted, urging commandments, remembrance, and faith in Christ and repentance. Nephi and Lehi preach through Nephite cities and among Lamanites, baptizing many. They are imprisoned, surrounded by fire, and a voice commands repentance; darkness disperses, angels minister, about three hundred witness, and many Lamanites lay down weapons and yield lands.

documents.text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 26:20** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records Paul’s defense before King Agrippa, with Festus and Bernice present. Paul recounts his Pharisaic life, persecution of believers, and his Damascus road encounter with Jesus, receiving a commission to witness to Jews and Gentiles. He states he preaches repentance and fulfillment of Moses and the prophets, including Christ’s suffering and resurrection. Festus challenges him; Agrippa responds. They conclude Paul is not guilty but is bound by his appeal to Caesar.

query: What is the role of the Holy Ghost?

documents.text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 14:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Jesus consoling his disciples, promising to prepare a place in the Father’s house and to return. He answers Thomas about the way to the Father, teaches Philip about seeing the Father through him, and promises believers will do works and have prayers answered in his name. He commands keeping his commandments, promises the Comforter/Holy Ghost, gives peace, foretells his departure, and mentions the prince of this world.

documents.text: To preach my gospel by the Spirit, even the Comforter which was sent forth to teach the truth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 50:14** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 46 verses and records the Lord warning elders about false spirits, hypocrisy, and deception in the church. It instructs that preaching and receiving must be by the Spirit of truth, and that what does not edify is not of God. It teaches testing spirit manifestations by prayer in Jesus’s name and acting without railing. It promises increasing light, purification, and authority, calls Wakefield, Pratt, and Corrill to strengthen churches, corrects Partridge, and exhorts watchfulness.

documents.text: And the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and the Father giveth the Holy Ghost unto the children of men, because of me.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 28:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records Jesus asking the Nephite disciples what they desire after his departure. Nine request to end their ministry and come to him at age seventy-two; three desire to remain and bring souls to Christ and are promised they will not taste death. They are transfigured, forbidden to reveal what they see, and continue ministering, baptizing, and giving the Holy Ghost. They escape prisons, pits, furnaces, and beasts unharmed; Mormon notes their future ministry among Gentiles, Jews, and Israel and explains their bodily change until judgment."
**Verse**: "And the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and the Father giveth the Holy Ghost unto the children of men, because of me."

documents.text: And it shall come to pass, that if you shall ask the Father in my name, in faith believing, you shall receive the Holy Ghost, which giveth utterance, that you may stand as a witness of the things of which you shall both hear and see, and also that you may declare repentance unto this generation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 14:8** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord declaring a great work coming forth and urging heed to His word. It calls willing laborers to harvest and promises salvation for enduring and keeping commandments. It commands seeking to establish Zion, asking in faith, and receiving the Holy Ghost to witness and declare repentance. Jesus Christ identifies Himself and states He will bring the fulness of the gospel from the Gentiles to Israel, calling David to assist.

documents.text: Therefore it is given to abide in you; the record of heaven; the Comforter; the peaceable things of immortal glory; the truth of all things; that which quickeneth all things, which maketh alive all things; that which knoweth all things, and hath all power according to wisdom, mercy, truth, justice, and judgment.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:61** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: To some it is given by the Holy Ghost to know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and that he was crucified for the sins of the world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 46:13** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records instructions for church meetings to be conducted by the Holy Spirit, commanding members not to exclude people from public, sacrament, or confirmation meetings, with restrictions on partaking after trespass until reconciliation. It warns against deception and commands prayer and thanksgiving. It lists spiritual gifts (testimony of Christ, belief, administration, operations, wisdom, knowledge, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning, tongues, interpretation) and assigns leaders to discern gifts.

documents.text: The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 121:46** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 46 verses and records a plea to God regarding persecutions, followed by comfort that adversity is temporary and endurance brings exaltation. It pronounces woes and judgments on those who falsely accuse, oppress, and murder the Saints, including loss of priesthood rights. It promises revealed knowledge in the dispensation of the fulness of times and teaches that priesthood power operates only through righteousness, persuasion, meekness, charity, and without compulsion."
**Verse**: "The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever."

documents.text: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Luke 12:12** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 59 verses and records Jesus warning disciples against Pharisaic hypocrisy, urging fear of God, confession of him, and reliance on the Holy Ghost in trials. He refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute, warns against covetousness, and gives the parable of the rich fool. He teaches not to worry, to seek God’s kingdom, give alms, and be watchful like servants. He speaks of accountability, coming division, discerning the times, and reconciling with an adversary before judgment."
**Verse**: "For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say."

documents.text: Ask the Father in my name in faith, believing that you shall receive, and you shall have the Holy Ghost, which manifesteth all things which are expedient unto the children of men.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 18:18** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 47 verses and records revelation to Oliver Cowdery and David Whitmer affirming the truth of their writings and commanding reliance on what is written to found Christ’s church. It commands repentance, faith, hope, and charity; taking upon Christ’s name; and baptism with enduring to the end. It discusses the worth of souls, Christ’s suffering and resurrection, and calls for selecting Twelve disciples to preach, baptize, and ordain priests and teachers."
**Verse**: "Ask the Father in my name in faith, believing that you shall receive, and you shall have the Holy Ghost, which manifesteth all things which are expedient unto the children of men."

documents.text: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 14:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Jesus consoling his disciples, promising to prepare a place in the Father’s house and to return. He answers Thomas about the way to the Father, teaches Philip about seeing the Father through him, and promises believers will do works and have prayers answered in his name. He commands keeping his commandments, promises the Comforter/Holy Ghost, gives peace, foretells his departure, and mentions the prince of this world.

documents.text: And this is my gospel—repentance and baptism by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, even the Comforter, which showeth all things, and teacheth the peaceable things of the kingdom.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 39:6** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 24 verses and records Jesus Christ identifying himself and defining his gospel as repentance, water baptism, and baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It addresses James, calls him to be baptized, preach the fulness of the gospel, labor in the vineyard, build the Church, and help bring forth Zion. It directs him to go to Ohio, urges gathering there, calls for missionary labor and repentance, and commands baptism and laying on of hands for the Holy Ghost in preparation for Christ’s coming."
**Verse**: "And this is my gospel—repentance and baptism by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, even the Comforter, which showeth all things, and teacheth the peaceable things of the kingdom."

documents.text: Wherefore, I now send upon you another Comforter, even upon you my friends, that it may abide in your hearts, even the Holy Spirit of promise; which other Comforter is the same that I promised unto my disciples, as is recorded in the testimony of John.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 88:3** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 141 verses and records the Lord’s instructions to assembled elders about the Holy Spirit of promise, the light of Christ, resurrection, and laws governing celestial, terrestrial, and telestial kingdoms. It describes earth’s sanctification and cosmic order, gives a parable of laborers, and commands prayer, sanctification, study, and organizing a school and house of God. It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

documents.text: For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 32:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records Nephi teaching what to do after entering “the way”: receive the Holy Ghost, which enables speaking with the tongue of angels and brings the words of Christ. He commands readers to feast on Christ’s words, ask and knock for understanding, and states this is the doctrine of Christ until Christ manifests in the flesh. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions."
**Verse**: "For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do."

documents.text: The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 130:22** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records teachings about seeing the Savior as a man, continued sociality after this life, and a personal appearing of the Father and Son. It addresses differing reckoning of time by planets, angels ministering only to their own earth, and God’s residence as a Urim and Thummim; the sanctified earth and individual white stones function similarly. It includes prophecy of bloodshed beginning in South Carolina, a statement about Joseph Smith possibly seeing the Son of Man, principles of intelligence gained in mortality, blessings tied to obedience to law, and the embodied nature of the Father and Son versus the Holy Ghost."
**Verse**: "The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us."

documents.text: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 15:26** from the **New Testament**. query: What does scripture teach about charity?

query: What is the covenant of baptism?

documents.text: Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?

Alma ordains priests and commands repentance, faith, unity, Sabbath observance, weekly worship, self-supporting priests, and giving to the needy. King Noah discovers them, sends an army, and Alma leads about 450 people into the wilderness.

documents.text: But whoso breaketh this covenant after he hath received it, and altogether turneth therefrom, shall not have forgiveness of sins in this world nor in the world to come.

documents.text: And again, by way of commandment to the church concerning the manner of baptism—All those who humble themselves before God, and desire to be baptized, and come forth with broken hearts and contrite spirits, and witness before the church that they have truly repented of all their sins, and are willing to take upon them the name of Jesus Christ, having a determination to serve him to the end, and truly manifest by their works that they have received of the Spirit of Christ unto the remission of their sins, shall be received by baptism into his church.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 20:37** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. He defines baptism as for accountable sinners unto remission of sins and warns against perverting this doctrine. He also mentions conflict with the Lamanites and Nephite pride, spiritual decline, and impending destruction.

It urges guarding speech, doing good, seeking peace, and trusting God amid suffering for righteousness, with readiness to answer for hope. It recounts Christ’s suffering, proclamation to spirits in prison, Noah’s ark, baptism, and Christ’s exaltation.

query: What does scripture say about obedience?

documents.text: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Hebrews 13:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and covers exhortations to continue brotherly love, show hospitality, remember prisoners, honor marriage, avoid covetousness, and trust God’s help. It urges respect for spiritual leaders and avoidance of strange doctrines. It references Jesus suffering outside the gate, seeking a future city, offering praise and doing good. The writer requests prayer, mentions Timothy’s release, sends greetings, and gives a benediction.

documents.text: And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Corinthians 10:6** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records Paul’s appeal to the Corinthians with Christlike meekness while defending his authority. He contrasts spiritual warfare with carnal methods, describing weapons that overthrow strongholds and bring thoughts into obedience. Paul addresses criticism of his weak presence, warns he will act firmly if needed, rejects self-commendation, limits boasting to his God-given measure, plans wider gospel preaching, and states approval comes from the Lord.

documents.text: Ye shall walk after the LORD your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 13:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records laws against apostasy and idolatry. It commands Israel not to heed prophets or dreamers whose signs lead to other gods, but to fear and obey the LORD. It requires execution of close relatives or friends who entice to idolatry. It orders investigation of an apostate city and, if confirmed, its destruction, burning of spoil, and prohibition of rebuilding.

documents.text: Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the LORD thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command thee this day.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 27:10** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Moses, the elders, priests, and Levites commanding Israel to keep the law after crossing the Jordan. They instruct setting up plastered stones on Mount Ebal, writing the law on them, building an uncut-stone altar, and offering burnt and peace offerings. Tribes stand on Gerizim and Ebal for blessings and curses, and Levites pronounce curses for idolatry, dishonoring parents, injustice, sexual sins, violence, bribery, and failing to keep the law.

documents.text: But if ye will not obey the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall the hand of the LORD be against you, as it was against your fathers.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 12:15** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Samuel’s address to Israel after appointing a king. Samuel asks the people to testify that he has not defrauded or oppressed them, and they affirm it. He recounts the LORD’s deliverances from Egypt and through judges, notes Israel’s request for a king when Nahash threatens, and warns obedience brings favor while rebellion brings judgment. Samuel calls thunder and rain at wheat harvest; the people fear and ask prayer. Samuel urges wholehearted service and warns both people and king face destruction if they persist in wickedness.

documents.text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 15:22** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Samuel commanding Saul to destroy Amalek completely. Saul musters Israel at Telaim, warns the Kenites to depart, defeats Amalek from Havilah to Shur, but spares King Agag and the best livestock. God tells Samuel he rejects Saul for disobedience. Samuel confronts Saul at Gilgal, declares obedience above sacrifice, and announces the kingdom is torn from Saul. Samuel executes Agag, returns to Ramah, and no longer visits Saul.

documents.text: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:6** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling.

documents.text: And shalt return unto the LORD thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul;

It states the commandment is accessible and near. Moses sets before them life and death, blessing and curse, urges choosing life by loving and obeying the LORD, warning against idolatry and perishing.

documents.text: That thou mayest love the LORD thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

documents.text: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass, if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love the LORD your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,

documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 28:1** from the **Old Testament**. It then lists curses for disobedience: disease, drought, crop failure, defeat, oppression, loss of family and property, foreign invasion and siege, cannibalism, plagues, reduced numbers, scattering among nations, and return to Egypt in captivity.

query: What is the plan of salvation?

documents.text: And now, behold, I say unto you: This is the plan of salvation unto all men, through the blood of mine Only Begotten, who shall come in the meridian of time.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Moses 6:62** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth."
**Verse**: "And now, behold, I say unto you: This is the plan of salvation unto all men, through the blood of mine Only Begotten, who shall come in the meridian of time."

documents.text: For it is expedient that an atonement should be made; for according to the great plan of the Eternal God there must be an atonement made, or else all mankind must unavoidably perish; yea, all are hardened; yea, all are fallen and are lost, and must perish except it be through the atonement which it is expedient should be made.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: For behold, if Adam had put forth his hand immediately, and partaken of the tree of life, he would have lived forever, according to the word of God, having no space for repentance; yea, and also the word of God would have been void, and the great plan of salvation would have been frustrated.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Alma 42:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching."
**Verse**: "For behold, if Adam had put forth his hand immediately, and partaken of the tree of life, he would have lived forever, according to the word of God, having no space for repentance; yea, and also the word of God would have been void, and the great plan of salvation would have been frustrated."

documents.text: O how great the plan of our God! documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 9:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jacob teaching about the Lord’s covenants with Israel, the fall, death, resurrection, and an infinite atonement. He describes judgment, paradise, hell, and restoration of body and spirit. He commands repentance, faith, baptism, and enduring to the end, explains accountability under law, pronounces woes on specific sins, and urges humility, prayer, and coming to the Holy One of Israel.

documents.text: We believe that through the Atonement of Christ, all mankind may be saved, by obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Gospel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Articles of Faith 1:3** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.

documents.text: But God did call on men, in the name of his Son, (this being the plan of redemption which was laid) saying: If ye will repent, and harden not your hearts, then will I have mercy upon you, through mine Only Begotten Son;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:33** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. He teaches resurrection and judgment by works, including a second spiritual death for the unrepentant. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: I say, that this is the man who receiveth salvation, through the atonement which was prepared from the foundation of the world for all mankind, which ever were since the fall of Adam, or who are, or who ever shall be, even unto the end of the world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 4:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. Benjamin commands belief in God, repentance, humility, prayer, and steadfast faith. He instructs them to live peaceably, teach children, and succor the poor by sharing substance, feeding, clothing, and visiting the sick, in wisdom and order, returning borrowed goods, watching thoughts, words, and deeds, and keeping commandments to avoid perishing.

documents.text: That through his atonement, and by obedience to the principles of the gospel, mankind might be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 138:4** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 60 verses and records Joseph F. Smith’s 1918 vision of the spirit world while pondering 1 Peter. He sees righteous spirits assembled awaiting Christ, who preaches resurrection and redemption to them. Christ does not visit the wicked but commissions righteous messengers to preach repentance, faith, and vicarious ordinances to spirits in darkness. Adam, Eve, Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, prophets, Nephite prophets, and latter-day leaders are present; temple work and continued missionary labor among the dead are described.

query: How do the Bible and Book of Mormon both describe the Messiah?

documents.text: And the Lord said: Blessed is he through whose seed Messiah shall come; for he saith—I am Messiah, the King of Zion, the Rock of Heaven, which is broad as eternity; whoso cometh in at the gate and climbeth up by me shall never fall; wherefore, blessed are they of whom I have spoken, for they shall come forth with songs of everlasting joy.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 7:53** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 69 verses and records Enoch’s visions and prophecy from Mahujah and mount Simeon, including peoples of Shum and Canaan, lands shown, and the command to preach repentance and baptize. It describes Zion becoming one heart, the City of Holiness, and being taken into heaven. Enoch sees Satan’s power, God and Enoch weeping, the Flood with Noah, the Son of Man’s crucifixion and resurrection, last-days tribulations, the New Jerusalem, and a millennial rest.

documents.text: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief; and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 14:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 12 verses and records Isaiah’s prophecy of the Lord’s servant: he grows up without comeliness, is despised and rejected, bears griefs and sorrows, is wounded for others’ transgressions, and is likened to a lamb led to slaughter without protest. It describes his unjust cutting off, burial with the wicked and rich, being an offering for sin, justifying many, and being rewarded after bearing sins and interceding for transgressors.

documents.text: Wherefore, how great the importance to make these things known unto the inhabitants of the earth, that they may know that there is no flesh that can dwell in the presence of God, save it be through the merits, and mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah, who layeth down his life according to the flesh, and taketh it again by the power of the Spirit, that he may bring to pass the resurrection of the dead, being the first that should rise.
documents.context:

It covers law, sin, and atonement; opposition in all things; creation and the Fall of Adam and Eve; the devil’s role; probation and repentance. Lehi teaches human agency to choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death, and urges obedience to the Mediator’s commandments."
**Verse**: "Wherefore, how great the importance to make these things known unto the inhabitants of the earth, that they may know that there is no flesh that can dwell in the presence of God, save it be through the merits, and mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah, who layeth down his life according to the flesh, and taketh it again by the power of the Spirit, that he may bring to pass the resurrection of the dead, being the first that should rise."

It covers last-days coming forth of a sealed book and the role of Gentiles, warnings against pride, false churches, and secret combinations, and commandments against priestcraft, murder, lying, theft, contention, and sexual sin, stating all are invited to salvation."
**Verse**: "And after the Messiah shall come there shall be signs given unto my people of his birth, and also of his death and resurrection; and great and terrible shall that day be unto the wicked, for they shall perish; and they perish because they cast out the prophets, and the saints, and stone them, and slay them; wherefore the cry of the blood of the saints shall ascend up to God from the ground against them."

documents.text: And it came to pass after my father had spoken these words he spake unto my brethren concerning the gospel which should be preached among the Jews, and also concerning the dwindling of the Jews in unbelief. And after they had slain the Messiah, who should come, and after he had been slain he should rise from the dead, and should make himself manifest, by the Holy Ghost, unto the Gentiles.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 10:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Lehi prophesying of Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, the Jews’ return, and the coming Messiah about six hundred years after leaving Jerusalem. He mentions prophets testifying, a forerunner who baptizes in Bethabara beyond Jordan, and the Messiah’s death and resurrection with manifestation to Gentiles by the Holy Ghost. It covers Israel scattered and gathered like an olive tree. Nephi desires revelation and warns of judgment and uncleanness.

documents.text: And not many days hence the Son of God shall come in his glory; and his glory shall be the glory of the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace, equity, and truth, full of patience, mercy, and long-suffering, quick to hear the cries of his people and to answer their prayers.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 9:26** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Alma, commanded by God, preaching again in Ammonihah with Amulek. The people contend, question his authority, and attempt to seize him. Alma recounts Lehi’s deliverance, warns that prosperity depends on keeping commandments, and calls them to repent or face destruction, including invasion by Lamanites. He cites angelic warnings and prophesies the Son of God’s coming to redeem the repentant. The Lord prevents Alma’s imprisonment; Amulek begins preaching.

documents.text: And he shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning; and his mother shall be called Mary.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 3:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. It covers the atonement for Adam’s transgression and ignorant sin, and requires repentance and faith for willful rebellion. It notes the law of Moses as types of Christ, declares little children blameless, describes yielding to the Holy Spirit, and warns of judgment and punishment for evil works.

Adam is commanded not to eat the forbidden tree, names animals, and Eve is created from his rib; marriage is instituted.

documents.text: And the Gods formed man from the dust of the ground, and took his spirit (that is, the man's spirit), and put it into him; and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.

It includes the command not to eat the forbidden tree, the creation of woman from Adam’s rib, marriage, nakedness without shame, and Adam naming animals.

documents.text: And the Gods said: Let us prepare the waters to bring forth abundantly the moving creatures that have life; and the fowl, that they may fly above the earth in the open expanse of heaven.

query: What do scriptures say about prophets being rejected?

documents.text: And it came to pass that the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection, for the people sought to destroy them.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Ether 11:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records prophets warning King Com’s people to repent; the people reject them and seek to kill them, so they flee to Com. It recounts reigns and conflicts under Shiblom, Seth, Ahah, Ethem, Moron, and Coriantor, including wars, famine, pestilence, and executions of prophets. Secret combinations fuel rebellions, overthrows, and long captivities. Prophets also foretell utter destruction and another people possessing the land. Coriantor begets Ether."
**Verse**: "And it came to pass that the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection, for the people sought to destroy them."

documents.text: For behold, the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. For behold, ye have closed your eyes, and ye have rejected the prophets; and your rulers, and the seers hath he covered because of your iniquity.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 27:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records prophecies about Gentiles and Jews in the last days, divine judgments, and nations fighting Zion. It describes the coming forth of a sealed book, its delivery to an unlearned man, and the role of three and other witnesses. It notes the learned refuse to read a sealed book, and the Lord commands the sealed portion kept. It covers a “marvelous work,” exposure of secret works, and future restoration where the deaf and blind receive understanding and Jacob’s children sanctify God."
**Verse**: "For behold, the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. For behold, ye have closed your eyes, and ye have rejected the prophets; and your rulers, and the seers hath he covered because of your iniquity."

documents.text: For behold, they have rejected the words of the prophets. Wherefore, if my father should dwell in the land after he hath been commanded to flee out of the land, behold, he would also perish. Wherefore, it must needs be that he flee out of the land.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Nephi 3:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Lehi’s dream commanding Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem for Laban’s brass plates containing Jewish records and their genealogy. Nephi agrees; the brothers travel to Jerusalem. Laman’s request is rejected and threatened. They offer their family riches; Laban attempts to kill them and seizes the property. Laman and Lemuel beat Nephi and Sam; an angel commands them to return and promises deliverance."
**Verse**: "For behold, they have rejected the words of the prophets. Wherefore, if my father should dwell in the land after he hath been commanded to flee out of the land, behold, he would also perish. Wherefore, it must needs be that he flee out of the land."

documents.text: And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Zechariah 13:3** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records a fountain opened for the house of David and Jerusalem for sin and uncleanness, the cutting off of idols, prophets, and an unclean spirit from the land, and punishment of false prophecy. It mentions prophets denying their role and explaining wounds. The LORD calls for the shepherd to be struck and the sheep scattered; two-thirds die, and a remnant is refined and acknowledged as God’s people.

documents.text: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 4:24** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 44 verses and records Jesus’ forty-day temptation in the wilderness and his Scripture responses. It covers his return to Galilee, teaching in synagogues, and reading Isaiah in Nazareth, declaring its fulfillment, and being rejected and threatened. It describes ministry in Capernaum: casting out an unclean spirit, healing Simon’s mother-in-law and many sick, silencing demons, withdrawing to a desert place, and continuing to preach in Galilee.

documents.text: And the Lord will surely prepare a way for his people, unto the fulfilling of the words of Moses, which he spake, saying: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you. And it shall come to pass that all those who will not hear that prophet shall be cut off from among the people.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 22:20** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Nephi explaining Isaiah’s words to his brothers, saying Israel is scattered among nations and later gathered through Gentile nursing and a mighty Gentile nation on the promised land. He describes the Lord revealing covenants, bringing Israel from captivity, and opposing the great and abominable church. Nephi recounts judgments of fire and conflict, identifies Moses’s prophet as the Holy One of Israel, warns against corrupt churches, and urges repentance, obedience, and enduring.

documents.text: Behold ye are worse than they; for as the Lord liveth, if a prophet come among you and declareth unto you the word of the Lord, which testifieth of your sins and iniquities, ye are angry with him, and cast him out and seek all manner of ways to destroy him; yea, you will say that he is a false prophet, and that he is a sinner, and of the devil, because he testifieth that your deeds are evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:26** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: And they that kill the prophets, and the saints, the depths of the earth shall swallow them up, saith the Lord of Hosts; and mountains shall cover them, and whirlwinds shall carry them away, and buildings shall fall upon them and crush them to pieces and grind them to powder.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 26:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records Nephi’s prophecy of Christ’s post-resurrection appearance to his people, signs of the Messiah, and destructions upon the wicked, followed by a period of peace for the righteous and later destruction. It covers last-days coming forth of a sealed book and the role of Gentiles, warnings against pride, false churches, and secret combinations, and commandments against priestcraft, murder, lying, theft, contention, and sexual sin, stating all are invited to salvation.

documents.text: Yea, wo unto this people, because of this time which has arrived, that ye do cast out the prophets, and do mock them, and cast stones at them, and do slay them, and do all manner of iniquity unto them, even as they did of old time.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:24** from the **Book of Mormon**. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ.
