documents.text: Because they have not hearkened to my words, saith the LORD, which I sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them; but ye would not hear, saith the LORD.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 29:19** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records Jeremiah’s letter from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon, sent by Elasah and Gemariah. It commands them to build houses, plant gardens, marry, increase, and seek Babylon’s peace, rejecting false prophets. It promises return after seventy years. It warns those remaining in Jerusalem of sword, famine, and pestilence. It condemns Ahab and Zedekiah for false prophecy and immorality, and Shemaiah for opposing Jeremiah, pronouncing punishment on him and his descendants.

documents.text: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the LORD.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 23:16** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records the LORD’s woe against corrupt pastors who scatter the flock, with a promise to gather a remnant and appoint new shepherds. It foretells a righteous Branch from David who reigns in justice and brings safety to Judah and Israel. It denounces profane prophets and priests in Samaria and Jerusalem, condemns false visions and dreams, warns of coming judgment, and forbids using the phrase “burden of the LORD,” threatening punishment and exile.

documents.text: And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ezekiel 14:10** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records elders coming to Ezekiel, and the LORD condemning idolatry in the heart and commanding Israel and sojourners to repent. It states God answers idolaters and cuts off those who seek prophets while clinging to idols, and that deceived prophets share punishment. It lists four judgments—famine, beasts, sword, pestilence—and says Noah, Daniel, and Job would save only themselves. A remnant from Jerusalem remains.

documents.text: Wherefore, he shall bring forth his words unto them, which words shall judge them at the last day, for they shall be given them for the purpose of convincing them of the true Messiah, who was rejected by them; and unto the convincing of them that they need not look forward any more for a Messiah to come, for there should not any come, save it should be a false Messiah which should deceive the people; for there is save one Messiah spoken of by the prophets, and that Messiah is he who should be rejected of the Jews.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 25:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Nephi explaining Isaiah’s writings and Jewish prophecy, and warning of God’s judgments on nations. Nephi prophesies the Jews’ destruction, Babylonian captivity, return to Jerusalem, later wars, rejection and crucifixion of the Messiah, and Jerusalem’s destruction and scattering. He states the Messiah comes 600 years after Lehi leaves Jerusalem and is Jesus Christ. Nephi teaches salvation through Christ, preservation of the record, grace, and keeping Moses’s law until fulfilled."
**Verse**: "Wherefore, he shall bring forth his words unto them, which words shall judge them at the last day, for they shall be given them for the purpose of convincing them of the true Messiah, who was rejected by them; and unto the convincing of them that they need not look forward any more for a Messiah to come, for there should not any come, save it should be a false Messiah which should deceive the people; for there is save one Messiah spoken of by the prophets, and that Messiah is he who should be rejected of the Jews."

documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Chronicles 36:16** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records Judah’s final kings: Jehoahaz is deposed by Egypt; Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah reign and do evil. Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon takes captives and temple vessels. Judah’s leaders reject prophets, and Jerusalem and the temple are destroyed; survivors serve in Babylon for seventy years. Cyrus of Persia proclaims return and rebuilding in Jerusalem.

documents.text: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 13:57** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 58 verses and records Jesus teaching multitudes by the sea in parables: the sower, tares among wheat, mustard seed, leaven, hidden treasure, pearl of great price, and a net. He explains why he uses parables and interprets the sower and tares to the disciples, including end-of-world separation by angels. He returns to his country, faces offense and unbelief, and does few mighty works.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive:

It forbids adopting Canaanite practices such as child sacrifice, divination, sorcery, and consulting spirits. It promises a prophet like Moses to whom Israel must listen, sets penalties for false prophets, and gives a test: unfulfilled words are not from the LORD.

documents.text: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honour in his own country.

The woman testifies, and many Samaritans believe; Jesus stays two days. In Galilee he returns to Cana and heals a nobleman’s son in Capernaum by word.

documents.text: Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them.

This chapter contains 30 verses and records a warning for Benjamin to flee Jerusalem as destruction comes from the north, with siege preparations against Zion. A northern nation attacks, bringing fear and mourning; Judah is tested like metal and called rejected silver."
**Verse**: "Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them."

documents.text: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 6:4** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 56 verses and records Jesus teaching in his hometown synagogue and being rejected, healing a few, and traveling to teach. Jesus sends the twelve out in pairs with instructions, and they preach repentance, cast out demons, and heal. Herod hears of Jesus and the chapter recounts John the Baptist’s imprisonment and beheading. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea, reaches Gennesaret, and heals many who touch him.

query: How is the gathering of Israel described across scripture?

documents.text: And verily I say unto you, I give unto you a sign, that ye may know the time when these things shall be about to take place—that I shall gather in, from their long dispersion, my people, O house of Israel, and shall establish again among them my Zion;
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 21:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 29 verses and records Jesus giving a sign of the Father’s work to gather scattered Israel and reestablish Zion. He says the revealed words come to Gentiles, who are commanded to repent, believe, and be baptized or be cut off. A protected servant brings forth the message. The remnant of Jacob is among Gentiles; judgments remove warfare, idolatry, and wickedness. Repentant Gentiles join the covenant, help build New Jerusalem, and assist the gathering from all nations.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass that my people, which are of the house of Israel, shall be gathered home unto the lands of their possessions; and my word also shall be gathered in one. And I will show unto them that fight against my word and against my people, who are of the house of Israel, that I am God, and that I covenanted with Abraham that I would remember his seed forever.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 29:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 14 verses and records the Lord’s purpose to remember covenants and recover Israel, sending forth additional scripture. It addresses Gentiles who claim the Bible is sufficient, reminding them the Bible comes through the Jews and warning against cursing them. It states God speaks to many nations and commands all peoples to write his words, which will judge the world. It foretells shared records among Jews, Nephites, and lost tribes, and Israel’s gathering."
**Verse**: "And it shall come to pass that my people, which are of the house of Israel, shall be gathered home unto the lands of their possessions; and my word also shall be gathered in one. And I will show unto them that fight against my word and against my people, who are of the house of Israel, that I am God, and that I covenanted with Abraham that I would remember his seed forever."

documents.text: And it shall come to pass that they shall be gathered in from their long dispersion, from the isles of the sea, and from the four parts of the earth; and the nations of the Gentiles shall be great in the eyes of me, saith God, in carrying them forth to the lands of their inheritance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 10:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Jacob teaching that Christ comes among the Jews and is crucified, followed by judgments, scattering, and later restoration when they believe. It covers Gentile involvement in gathering Israel, promises about a land of inheritance, liberty without kings, and God’s protection of Zion. Jacob urges repentance, freedom to choose life or death, reconciliation to God, and salvation through grace, resurrection, and atonement.

documents.text: And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ezekiel 37:21** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 28 verses and describes Ezekiel’s vision of a valley of dry bones revived by prophecy and breath, explained as Israel restored and returned to its land. It records the sign of two sticks for Judah and Joseph joined as one, symbolizing reunification. The LORD promises gathering from nations, one king “David,” cleansing from idols, obedience to statutes, an everlasting covenant of peace, and a permanent sanctuary among them.

documents.text: And then will I gather them in from the four quarters of the earth; and then will I fulfil the covenant which the Father hath made unto all the people of the house of Israel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 16:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Jesus saying he has other sheep elsewhere and will visit them by the Father’s command. He commands the Nephites to write his words to be preserved and manifested to the Gentiles, bringing scattered Israel to knowledge and a gathering. It blesses believing Gentiles, warns unbelieving Gentiles, and states the gospel will return to Israel. It affirms this land as Israel’s inheritance and quotes Isaiah about Zion’s restoration.

documents.text: And as surely as the Lord liveth, will he gather in from the four quarters of the earth all the remnant of the seed of Jacob, who are scattered abroad upon all the face of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 5:24** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records the Nephites’ full belief in prophets’ words, their repentance, and the capture and judgment of robbers, freeing those who covenant to stop murdering. It notes 25 years passing with many events not recorded. Mormon identifies himself, his record sources and plates, and states promises of blessing and future gathering and restoration of the house of Jacob and seed of Joseph through Jesus Christ.

documents.text: Wherefore, he will bring them again out of captivity, and they shall be gathered together to the lands of their inheritance; and they shall be brought out of obscurity and out of darkness; and they shall know that the Lord is their Savior and their Redeemer, the Mighty One of Israel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 22:12** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Nephi explaining Isaiah’s words to his brothers, saying Israel is scattered among nations and later gathered through Gentile nursing and a mighty Gentile nation on the promised land. He describes the Lord revealing covenants, bringing Israel from captivity, and opposing the great and abominable church. Nephi recounts judgments of fire and conflict, identifies Moses’s prophet as the Holy One of Israel, warns against corrupt churches, and urges repentance, obedience, and enduring.

documents.text: And then shall the remnants, which shall be scattered abroad upon the face of the earth, be gathered in from the east and from the west, and from the south and from the north; and they shall be brought to the knowledge of the Lord their God, who hath redeemed them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 20:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 46 verses and records Jesus ending vocal prayer, instructing continual prayer in the heart, and miraculously providing and administering bread and wine to disciples and the multitude. He teaches of his body and blood and speaks of fulfilling Isaiah and the Father’s covenants: gathering scattered Israel, establishing a New Jerusalem, Gentile blessings and judgment for impenitence, and Jerusalem’s future redemption and inheritance.

documents.text: And after the house of Israel should be scattered they should be gathered together again; or, in fine, after the Gentiles had received the fulness of the Gospel, the natural branches of the olive tree, or the remnants of the house of Israel, should be grafted in, or come to the knowledge of the true Messiah, their Lord and their Redeemer.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 10:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Lehi prophesying of Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, the Jews’ return, and the coming Messiah about six hundred years after leaving Jerusalem. He mentions prophets testifying, a forerunner who baptizes in Bethabara beyond Jordan, and the Messiah’s death and resurrection with manifestation to Gentiles by the Holy Ghost. It covers Israel scattered and gathered like an olive tree. Nephi desires revelation and warns of judgment and uncleanness.

documents.text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 21:12** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 16 verses and describes a rod and root of Jesse endowed with the Spirit of the Lord who judges righteously and slays the wicked. It records millennial peace among animals and safety on the Lord’s holy mountain. It covers an ensign sought by Gentiles, the Lord recovering Israel’s remnant from many lands, gathering Judah, ending Ephraim–Judah envy, subduing neighboring nations, drying waters for passage, and a highway from Assyria.

documents.text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Isaiah 11:12** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 16 verses and describes a Branch from Jesse endowed with the LORD’s Spirit who judges righteously and strikes the wicked. It records peace in the holy mountain where animals and children dwell safely and the earth is full of the LORD’s knowledge. It covers an ensign drawing Gentiles, the second recovery of Israel’s remnant from many lands, reunion of Ephraim and Judah, victories over neighboring peoples, and a dried river and highway for return.

documents.text: Yea, then will he remember the isles of the sea; yea, and all the people who are of the house of Israel, will I gather in, saith the Lord, according to the words of the prophet Zenos, from the four quarters of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 19:16** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 24 verses and records Nephi making plates of ore by commandment, explaining the division between sacred writings and other records, and directing that the plates be preserved and handed down. It quotes prophets Zenock, Neum, and Zenos about the Messiah’s coming, rejection, crucifixion, burial, and signs, and about Israel’s scattering and future gathering. Nephi teaches his brethren from the brass plates, Moses, and Isaiah, and applies Isaiah to them as a remnant.

documents.text: O ye house of Israel whom I have spared, how oft will I gather you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, if ye will repent and return unto me with full purpose of heart.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 10:6** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records the people’s silence after the voice from heaven, then a renewed voice calls the house of Israel to repent, promising gathering or desolation. After three days the darkness and earthquakes cease and survivors turn from mourning to praise of Jesus Christ. It states prophecies are fulfilled, the more righteous are spared, cites Zenos, Zenock, and Jacob, and foreshadows Christ’s manifestation to Nephites and spared Lamanites."
**Verse**: "O ye house of Israel whom I have spared, how oft will I gather you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, if ye will repent and return unto me with full purpose of heart."

documents.text: O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.

**Verse**: "O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you."
